subject: Steve Hilton hits Dem governor's 2028 pitch by calling out Newsom's rail record
posts:
Californians face billions wasted on a stalled bullet train while politicians trade 2028 presidential jabs on HBO.
Evidence: $126B projected cost, 2008 bond approval, consultant travel scandal.
#Aletheia #USPol #California

Dem governors claim proven infrastructure 'receipts' like high-speed rail to distinguish themselves for 2028.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good Potential

California's bullet train remains years behind schedule with billions spent and zero passenger tracks laid, fueling partisan attacks.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.7) — Exclusive Constraint

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. Political posturing over infrastructure success masks severe mismanagement and multi-billion-dollar overruns.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 1.9, z: 3)
Steve Hilton and Andy Beshear sparred over Democratic governance on Bill Maher's show, using California's troubled rail project as a political football.

The Bright Side:
Public scrutiny and independent audits are finally exposing consultant travel scandals and forcing fiscal accountability.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confuses political rhetorical branding (WHAT) with verified institutional delivery (WHO/WHERE), treating transit as a 2028 proxy war.

Social Physics Analysis:
Actors run a Smart Selfish Maneuver by weaponizing real infrastructure delays as a pretext for partisan branding, deflecting from systemic policy failures.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
Modal Dynamics: can be -> is not via Red Top (The Imperial Trap).
Promising visionary public transit yields systemic stasis and erasure.

The Unavoidable Truth: California's high-speed rail project suffers from massive cost overruns and severe scheduling delays.

The Unavoidable Lie: Partisan campaign ads imply that canceling the rail will instantly fix broader social crises.

Alethekanon:
Politicians trade visionary claims while taxpayers bear the cost of decades of administrative inertia and runaway budgets.

Awwthekanon:
It is heartbreaking for struggling families to watch billions vanish into unfinished concrete while basic essentials become unaffordable.

Brothekanon:
Classic political talk show theater—everyone argues about 2028 while nobody can actually ride a bullet train in California.

Spirithekanon:
"Dishonest scales are an abomination to the Lord, but an accurate weight is his delight." Proverbs 11:1 FAIL
Inflated promises and mismanaged public funds corrupt the sacred trust between citizens and stewards.

[Source 1 — www.foxnews.com] (URL: https://www.foxnews.com/media/steve-hilton-hits-dem-governors-2028-pitch-calling-out-newsoms-rail-record):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Steve Hilton hits Dem governor's 2028 pitch by calling out Newsom's rail record

California Gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton seized on Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear's boast about Democrat successes to criticize the struggling rail project under Gov. Gavin Newsom.

Actual Article Body:

Market data provided by Factset. Powered and implemented by FactSet Digital Solutions. Legal Statement. Mutual Fund and ETF data provided by LSEG.

Steve Hilton questioned California's unfinished high-speed rail project after Andy Beshear touted Democratic governors' accomplishments on HBO's 'Real Time with Bill Maher,' prompting Maher to agree.

Republican California gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton challenged Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear's argument that a Democratic governor should lead the party's 2028 presidential ticket Friday on HBO's "Real Time with Bill Maher," pointing to California Gov. Gavin Newsom's unfinished high-speed rail project as Beshear touted Democratic governors' accomplishments.

Beshear, discussing potential Democratic presidential contenders, argued that governors could point to tangible accomplishments that would distinguish them from President Donald Trump.

"What Democratic governors have are receipts," he said. "You can look at, have you built the housing?"

"Have you built the high-speed rail?" Hilton asked.

BILL MAHER CLASHES WITH NEWSOM OVER CALIFORNIA LEADERS, SAYS OTHER SIDE WILL ASK, ‘HAVE YOU SEEN THE STATS?'

Republican gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton challenged Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear's claims about Democratic governors' accomplishments, pointing to California's unfinished high-speed rail project during HBO's "Real Time with Bill Maher." (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News)

The exchange came after Maher raised Newsom as a potential 2028 contender, although the California governor has not formally announced a presidential campaign.

Maher acknowledged Hilton's point, suggesting the Republican candidate could use the project's troubled history against Newsom.

"You're going to have a field day with that. No, you're right," Maher said.

Matt Ciepielowski, Hilton's campaign manager, criticized California's continued investment in the project in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"If Andy Beshear thinks California’s high-speed rail is something to brag about, he should try buying a ticket. Billions spent, years behind schedule, and Californians still can’t ride it. Gavin Newsom’s answer is to keep pouring money into it."

Ciepielowski also said Hilton would end state funding for the project if elected governor.

"Steve Hilton will end state funding on day one," he said. "Californians are struggling to pay their own bills. They shouldn’t have to keep paying for Sacramento’s failures, too."

TRUMP BACKS HILTON AHEAD OF CALIFORNIA GOP VOTE, TESTING BIANCO’S GRIP ON PARTY ENDORSEMENT

Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear touted Democratic governors' "receipts" ahead of the 2028 presidential election before Steve Hilton questioned California's high-speed rail record, prompting agreement from host Bill Maher. (KC McGinnis/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

California state Sen. Tony Strickland, R-Huntington Beach, vice chair of the Senate Transportation Committee, also criticized Newsom's handling of the project, pointing to findings about taxpayer-funded travel expenses submitted by project consultants.

"The high-speed fail should have been defunded when Newsom took office in 2019," he said. "Instead, he doubled down on a project that will never be built as originally proposed to Californians. The latest scandal involving project consultants' misuse of public funds to pay for luxury travel under Newsom’s watch is yet another slap in the face to California families struggling to pay for essentials like gas, food, and rent."

"These are taxpayer dollars, yet project consultants treat them like their personal ATM. This project will go down as one of the most wasteful government projects in California history," he continued.

LIZ PEEK: CALIFORNIA VOTERS FED UP WITH DEMOCRATS MAY TURN TO STEVE HILTON FOR CHANGE

California state Sen. Tony Strickland criticized Gov. Gavin Newsom's handling of the high-speed rail project following an investigation that uncovered questionable taxpayer-funded travel expenses involving project consultants. (David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

California's high-speed rail system has faced years of delays and escalating costs since voters approved nearly $10 billion in bonds in 2008. An April estimate placed the cost of the full project at approximately $126 billion, compared with an original estimate of $33 billion. No high-speed track had been laid as of that report.

The California High-Speed Rail Authority said in its 2026 business plan that completing the initial Merced-to-Bakersfield segment would cost an estimated $35.7 billion, with passenger service targeted for 2033. According to the authority's financial records, approximately $15.7 billion had been spent through February.

The project's financial oversight also came under renewed scrutiny following a September investigation by California's independent high-speed rail inspector general. Investigators identified approximately $81,000 in consultant travel expenses that appeared to violate state regulations and another $543,000 that appeared impermissible under contract terms, with some overlap between the findings. Questionable charges included premium transportation and trips to gyms, a nightclub and an escape room.

The California High-Speed Rail Authority outlined corrective actions, including additional oversight, employee training and efforts to recover payments determined to be improper.

Despite the criticism, the California High-Speed Rail Authority has maintained that construction is advancing. In an October update, officials reported completing 66 major structures and nearly 90 miles of guideway in the Central Valley, while emphasizing the project's expected transportation, economic and employment benefits.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Fox News Digital reached out to Newsom and the California High-Speed Rail Authority for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

[Source 2 — nypost.com] (URL: https://nypost.com/2026/10/25/us-news/steve-hilton-unveils-his-vision-for-california-bullet-train/):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Steve Hilton unveils his vision for California bullet train

In an AI-generated ad, Steve Hilton imagines a future where the multibillion-dollar undertaking is transformed into a monument to government failure.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

California gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton is pitching a dramatic end to the state’s troubled high-speed rail project — imagining a future where the multibillion-dollar undertaking is transformed into a monument to government failure.

The Republican candidate’s AI-generated campaign ad, titled around his proposal to “cancel High Speed Rail, turn it into the Government Failures National Monument,” offers a stark before-and-after vision of California depending on who occupies the governor’s office.

The spot contrasts a sun-drenched, prosperous California under Hilton with a frozen, dystopian version of the Golden State under Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra, blaming the latter’s hypothetical administration for soaring gas prices, struggling businesses and worsening conditions on Skid Row.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Never miss a story

The ad opens with an AI-generated vision of California two years into a hypothetical Hilton administration, portraying the high-speed rail project as a “failed promise.” In the opening sequence, Skid Row is transformed into a luxurious destination resembling Rodeo Drive, complete with cherry blossoms and fine dining.

The Third Street Promenade in Santa Monica is bustling with shoppers, while gas prices have fallen to $3 a gallon and families are back on the road.

The narrator describes the rail project’s cancellation and transformation into a national monument, declaring: “Visitors come from around the world to see the most expensive piece of concrete in human history.”

The idyllic imagery then gives way to Hilton’s depiction of California under Becerra, with the ad claiming that gas prices would climb to $8 a gallon and families would struggle to afford driving.

The campaign’s sunny visuals abruptly turn dark and wintry, depicting an apparently deserted Third Street Promenade and a worsening public health crisis on Skid Row, where the narrator claims typhoid and rat infestations have overwhelmed emergency crews.

The ad also accuses Becerra of raising taxes to funnel another $200 billion into the rail project, which it derides as a “railroad to nowhere.”

The spot closes with a final transformation: sunlight returns to the bleak landscape as the narrator urges Californians to back Hilton.

“California’s future is still being written. Vote for Steve Hilton. Just try it,” the voice-over declares.

The ad targets one of California’s most expensive and politically contentious infrastructure projects.

The California High-Speed Rail Authority’s draft 2026 business plan estimated that completing the first phase of the 494-mile line between San Francisco and Los Angeles and Anaheim could cost approximately $231.3 billion under its full-buildout scenario. A revised approach puts the cost at roughly $126.2 billion.

The project was originally approved by voters in 2008, with an initial estimate of $33 billion and a target completion date of 2020. Construction and funding challenges have since forced repeated revisions to its projected cost and timeline.

Hilton has pledged to cancel the project entirely. Becerra, meanwhile, has said he would scrap its current configuration, though he has offered fewer details about his plans for the rail system, according to KPBS.

The two candidates are competing to succeed Gov. Gavin Newsom in the Nov. 3 election, with the race placing affordability, homelessness and the future of California’s government spending at the center of the campaign.
